description.value: An event-related fMRI study assessed brain activation to heroin-related versus neutral cues in short-term and long-term abstinent heroin-dependent patients, and examined abstinence-duration correlations.

value: We hypothesized that long-term abstinence would lead to decreases in the cue-induced craving as well as brain responses, especially in the prefrontal regions.

description.value: Cross-sectional study of abstinent heroin-dependent patients divided into short-term and long-term abstinence groups.

spans.text: In the present study, we used an event-related fMRI paradigm and cross-sectional design to investigate a cohort of abstinent heroin patients who varied in the duration of their abstinence.
In the present study, we used an event-related fMRI paradigm and cross-sectional design to investigate a cohort of abstinent heroin patients who varied in the duration of their abstinence.

Another limitation was that although this study employed a between-subject cross-sectional design rather than a within-subject longitudinal design, the investigation of the difference in the brain response to heroin-related cues as a function of abstinence duration would identify neurobiological characteristics related to successful abstinence.

spans.text: We used an event-related fMRI paradigm to measure brain activation in response to heroin cue-related pictures versus neutral pictures as the control condition in heroin-dependent patients undergoing short-term and long-term abstinence.
MRI was performed on a 3.0 T GE MRI system (General Electric, Milwaukee, Wisconsin) using an 8-channel phase array coil.

The functional images were collected using gradient Echo Planar Imaging (EPI) (TR = 2 s, TE = 30 ms, matrix = 64×64, FOV = 256×256 mm , slice thickness = 4 mm, gap = 0 mm and flip angle = 90 degrees) with in-plane resolution of 4×4 mm .

For each subject, 240 echo-planar volumes were collected respectively during the cue-reactivity run.
All subjects participated in a 490-s run during which they were exposed to 48 pictures (24 heroin pictures and 24 neutral pictures).
All of the abstinent patients met the criteria for heroin dependence for at least 1 year, as diagnosed by the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV.
The patients’ general cognitive function was assessed by an experienced doctor in the Drug Rehabilitation Center through a face-to-face interview.
